subject.title: [Feature]: First-class org/team deployment — workspace scaffolding, RBAC, and deployment manifests

question: Which org/team deployment boundary should OpenClaw core own first: scaffolding/manifests, per-session tool policy, conversation identity, multi-token gateway auth, or hostile tenant isolation?
rationale: The issue would define new public config and security contracts across Gateway auth, sessions, tool policy, workspaces, and deployment docs, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent trust boundary.

options.title: Decompose under this umbrella
options.body: Keep this issue open and approve narrow sub-issues only after the threat model, config shape, and upgrade contract are explicit.

options.title: Route setup outward
options.body: Keep core focused on missing auth/session/tool-policy APIs while workspace scaffolding and manifests live in plugins, docs, or external tooling.

options.title: Decline team mode for now
options.body: Document separate Gateways, trusted proxy, per-agent profiles, and current multi-agent routing as the supported isolation pattern.

recommendation.title: Decompose under this umbrella
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and approve narrow sub-issues only after the threat model, config shape, and upgrade contract are explicit.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history on scoped conversation capability profiles and gateway trust-model documentation adjacent to the requested boundary.
